# UC-379 — Triage the Sub-Order Queue by SLA Age

## Header Info
- **Use Case ID:** UC-379
- **Title:** Triage the Sub-Order Queue by SLA Age
- **Actor:** Vendor (ACT-02) — Owner/Editor/Manager staff
- **Trigger:** The vendor opens the sub-order queue to work the oldest orders first
- **Priority:** P2
- **Goal:** Order own sub-orders by SLA age so no confirmation silently crosses the 24-hour escalation.
- **Preconditions:** Own-store scope (BR-VND-07); queue readable (`GET /store/orders`, API-ORD-006); store active (BR-VND-04).

## Main Scenario
1. Vendor opens Orders → client `GET /store/orders?sort=slaAge_desc` returns own sub-orders with `state`, `placedAt`, `confirmDueAt` (API-ORD-006, BR-VND-07).
2. Server orders rows oldest `confirmDueAt` first and pages them offset-style with `pageSize` and `?status` filters (API-ORD-006).
3. Vendor works the head of the queue → client `POST /store/orders/{id}/confirm` (PLACED → CONFIRMED, API-ORD-008) or `POST /store/orders/{id}/processing` (API-ORD-009).
4. Each accepted action appends an `order_status_history` row with actor, timestamp and reason (BR-ORD-03).
5. A sub-order still `CONFIRMED` 24 h after confirmation is escalated to Admin review with a notification — never silently auto-cancelled (BR-ORD-10).
6. The escalated row leaves the vendor's actionable set; the vendor keeps working the next-oldest rows in the same view (API-ORD-006).

## Alternative Scenarios
- **A1 — Filter to one state:** `?status=PLACED` shows only unaccepted rows in the same SLA order; actions rejoin the main flow.
- **A2 — Row worked by a colleague:** a refetch shows the newer state and the row drops out of the actionable set (BR-ORD-03).
- **A3 — Escalation visible to Admin:** after 24 h the case appears in `GET /admin/orders` flagged `SLA_24H` while the vendor queue still shows its age (BR-ORD-10, API-ORD-013).

## Exception Scenarios
- **E1 — Stale row version:** confirm on a sub-order that already moved → 409 `STATE_CONFLICT`; history unchanged (BR-ORD-01, EC-14).
- **E2 — Suspended store:** the queue read fails with `STORE_SUSPENDED` and no rows are returned (BR-VND-04).
- **E3 — Foreign sub-order id:** → 404 `NOT_FOUND` before any action runs (BR-VND-07).

## Postconditions
- Worked rows advanced exactly one state with an append-only history entry; untouched rows keep their age (BR-ORD-03).
- A breached 24-hour SLA leaves the sub-order intact and flagged for Admin review — never auto-cancelled (BR-ORD-10).

## Business Rules Applied
- BR-ORD-01, BR-ORD-03, BR-ORD-10, BR-VND-04, BR-VND-07

## Related Requirements
- FR-012 (Order Lifecycle Management)
- Cross-reference: UC-019 accepts one sub-order manually; UC-375 starts fulfilment — both work the same aged queue.

## Permissions / Data / External Dependencies
- **Permissions:** own-store staff; each action follows its endpoint's role column (BR-VND-06) enforced server-side (SEC-REQ-004).
- **Data involved:** sub-order rows (`state`, `placedAt`, `confirmDueAt`, `version`), `order_status_history`.
- **External dependencies:** notification fan-out for the escalation alert (B10); Admin queue `GET /admin/orders` (B13).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC-UC379-01:** Given sub-orders of different ages, when the vendor sorts by SLA age, then the oldest `confirmDueAt` appears first (API-ORD-006).
- **AC-UC379-02:** Given a sub-order CONFIRMED for 24 h, when the deadline passes, then it is escalated to Admin review with a notification and is not auto-cancelled (BR-ORD-10).
- **AC-UC379-03:** Given another store's sub-order id, when the vendor opens it, then 404 `NOT_FOUND` is returned (BR-VND-07).
- **AC-UC379-04:** Given a sub-order that moved concurrently, when the vendor confirms it, then 409 `STATE_CONFLICT` is returned and history is unchanged (BR-ORD-01).
